limits: Filters rows as given; it does not re-rank or recompute them.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Selects rows by a condition; it computes no new quantity.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which rows of this table meet the condition, and how many were dropped?

description: Keep only the rows of a table-shaped output that meet a condition — the bands above a size, the guides over a score, the assays under a penalty. Emits the kept rows plus how many were dropped, so a downstream gate can act on the count.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

field.description: which field of each row to test (e.g. `size`, `score`, `length`). Leave empty to test the row itself when it is a plain number.

items.description: the rows to filter — wire a json/list output (bands, guides, assays, amplicons).

max.description: upper bound, inclusive. Only applies when operator is between.

min.description: lower bound, inclusive. Only applies when operator is between.

operator.description: how to compare. Values: == (equals), != (does not equal), > (greater than), >= (at least), < (less than), <= (at most), between (between (inclusive)), in (is one of), not_in (is none of), contains (contains text), is_true (is true), not_empty (is not empty).

set.description: the values the field must be one of (or none of). Only applies when operator is in or not_in.

text.description: the text a field must contain. Only applies when operator is contains.

value.description: the value to compare against. Only applies when operator is == or != or > or >= or < or <=.

name: filter_items

count.description: how many rows were kept — wire this into check_value to gate on it

items.description: the rows that met the condition
